images.title: Rhombus into rectangle
images.purpose: Shows the four right triangles of a rhombus rearranged into a rectangle of one diagonal by half the other.
images.composition: Before and after: rhombus on the left, rectangle on the right, one plain arrow between them.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, lots of empty space, the figure large and centred, thin dark outlines. Only the labels listed appear; no other text, no scenery, no characters. LEFT: a rhombus with a horizontal diagonal 12 units long and a vertical diagonal 8 units long, crossing at their midpoints at right angles (small right angle mark at the centre). Both diagonals drawn as grey (#6B7280) dashed lines, cutting the rhombus into 4 congruent right triangles with legs 6 and 4. The 2 triangles above the horizontal diagonal are filled teal (#0072B2); the 2 below are filled amber (#E69F00). Label 12 cm along the horizontal diagonal and 8 cm along the vertical diagonal. MIDDLE: one plain dark arrow pointing right. RIGHT: a rectangle 12 units wide and 4 units tall. Inside, the 2 teal triangles stand exactly as in the top half of the rhombus (together a triangle with base 12 and height 4); the 2 amber triangles are flipped up into the two empty top corners, one each side, filling the rectangle exactly. Label 12 cm under it, 4 cm beside it and 48 cm² below it. Check: 12 × 4 = 48 and 1/2 × 12 × 8 = 48.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A rhombus rearranges into a rectangle one diagonal long and half the other diagonal tall.
images.description: Shows the four right triangles of a rhombus rearranged into a rectangle of one diagonal by half the other.
images.context: Matches the worked example: diagonals 12 cm and 8 cm, area 48 cm². Dissection from the Sulba Sutras.
images.teaching_notes: Count the four triangles on both sides: 4 before, 4 after.

image_decisions.why: The dissection is the derivation; showing the before and after makes the side lengths readable.
